x: John Webb of Basildon A.C. ( more will be seen of this stylish walker in International events in the future) won the race in 51m.58. more than a minute in front of R.
Medals were not forthcoming for Belgrave in this year's Cambridge '7' at Bexley. Ray Middleton (54:34) was our only man up front, finishing sixth, 2:43 behind winner John Webb.
The weather in no way affected the times and although John Webb won in 50.57 Trowbridge's latest find John Kirk caused quite a sensation with his second place in 51.06.
Dominated by John Webb and Bob Hughes who were both fresh from Mexico the Bels were not up for individual honours but managed the team race without trouble.

The individual race at once developed into a scrap between Arthur Jones of Brighton and John Webb from Basildon. These two, both fresh from Mexico disputed the lead until the final hill where Jones pulled clear to finish a comfortable winner.

Pushed on by supporting John Webb I did all I could to nail him but with the sight of home ahead he just held me off. At first I felt disgusted at not catching him but he had walked well and that's all that counts in Walking.
John Webb,with Roger Mills in close pursuit, broke away. These positions were held to the finish to enable Webb to win his first National title at the age of 36.

Higher up the field Carl Lawton finished 3rd to Bob Dobson with John Bromley almost catching International John Webb. The two other Dunsfords were Babbette and Mrs. in the Girls and Ladies races respectively.
